thread:
claire: Quick RFC follow-up about the "compat lattice" idea — specifically tenant signalling for the API migration (v3 -> v4). TL;DR: do we require an explicit opt-in header (client-driven) or try server-side sniffing + telemetry (server-driven) to route to v3 behaviour?

raj: Prefer opt-in header for predictability. Server sniffing is brittle for edge cases and makes rollbacks hard.

maria: Agreed on predictability, but opt-in puts more burden on customers. Can we do a hybrid: header for tenants that know, server-detect + shadow-mode for others?

alex: Hybrid seems reasonable. Implementation idea: 1) Accept header X-RW-Compat: v3|v4 2) If missing, consult tenant flag in tenant-config (defaults to auto-detect) 3) Auto-detect runs a cheap probe and then writes a sticky decision per-tenant.

claire: Sticky per-tenant decision + ability to flip via Console sounds good. Two concerns: (a) rollout speed for large fleets, (b) telemetry clarity (we must know how often auto-detect misroutes).

raj: For (a) we can expose batch-set in the Console and a rollout API. For (b) add a mismatch counter and sampling of payloads to S3 for manual inspection.

maria: Also: graceful degradation rules. If v4 runtime fails for a request we should fall back to v3 for that tenant for N requests, then alert. Don't want persistent 500s.

sam: infra-bot: deploy check passed for the compat-lattice feature branch on staging.

alex: Example header we suggest: ``X-Redwood-Compat: v3``. Clients that ship polyfills can set this. For SDKs we should default to not setting header until the SDK bumps major.

claire: That raises SDK churn question. If we rely on header opt-in, SDKs must be updated. Can we provide client-side polyfill via middleware so app code doesn't change?

raj: Middleware helps but adoption will lag. We should provide both: an SDK middleware shim and server auto-detect. Migration plan: Week 0: announce and enable shadow-mode; Week 2: opt-in header available; Week 4: begin default switch for new tenants; Week 8: deprecate v3 for active tenants with reminders.

maria: Telemetry + alerting matrix: create dashboards for: "compat_mismatch_rate", "auto_detect_rollbacks", "per_tenant_fallbacks". Add a daily report email to eng-ops.

claire: UX note for Console: show a per-tenant timeline + current decision + override button. Also surface the probe sample.

raj: Security/KMS note: if payload shapes change and embeddings dims change, make sure the probe sampling strips PII before storing. Compliance needs an opt-out for sampling.

alex: Implementation details: routing layer changes in edge-proxy: add a header read path and a tenant-config lookup cache (TTL 5m). If header present, shortcut. If not, consult cache, otherwise call tenant-service (fast path) and record sticky decision.

maria: Performance note: cache miss cost must be <2ms p95. If not, fallback to conservative behaviour (route to v3) to avoid latency spikes.

claire: Decision proposal (checkable):
- Primary signal: X-Redwood-Compat header (explicit opt-in)
- Secondary: tenant-config sticky decision (set by Console or auto-detect probe)
- Safety: automatic fallback to v3 on error + per-tenant cooldown
- Observability: mismatch counters, sampled payload store (PII scrubbed), dashboards and daily report
- SDKs: provide middleware shim and docs; default not to set header until major bump

Please react with :+1: to accept or :question: to flag. If accepted we'll create an RFC follow-up with tasks for edge-proxy, tenant-service, console, telemetry, and SDK teams.

alex: :+1: from runtime side — we can do cache + header fast path this sprint.

raj: :+1: ops and rollout plan looks good. I'll own batch set API.

maria: :+1: will own telemetry dashboards and sampling pipeline.

sam: infra-bot: created ticket ARCH-1245 for edge-proxy change.

claire: Great. I'll author the follow-up RFC and split into tickets. Action items in thread: 1) alex - edge-proxy changes (ARCH-1245) 2) raj - batch-set API + tenant-config flags 3) maria - telemetry + scrub pipeline 4) SDK leads - middleware shim + docs.

alex: Quick note — add a canary rule to route 1% of traffic from new tenants to v4 to validate in prod before full default flip.

claire: Added canary to the plan. Thanks everyone.

infra-bot: Note: scheduled job "compat-probe" will run in staging at 2024-06-12T03:00:00Z.
